Part I — Vienna · 02Museum Booster · January 2026

Museum Connections, Paris

Launch communication for Museum Booster’s stand at Museum Connections in Paris: messaging, printed materials and the public introduction of the Museum Booster Academy.

Back to selected work

Preparation for Museum Booster’s stand at Museum Connections, the museum trade fair in Paris: the messaging, the printed materials and the launch assets the Museum Booster Academy needed for its first public appearance.

The concept on the stand is called Don’t Panic. Museum leaders work under shrinking budgets and public scrutiny, and most leadership programmes sell them urgency. This one does the opposite: reassurance first, then a clear invitation into four two-day workshops in Vienna.

The visual world for the expo borrowed from art the audience already knows: Edvard Munch’s The Scream became the face of Don’t Panic, and a still from Bernardo Bertolucci’s The Dreamers — the run through the Louvre — carried the same energy onto the materials we brought to the trade fair.

Part I — Vienna · 03Future Bridge · Public events in Vienna

What Matters Platform

Registration pages, newsletters, posters and AI motion loops for public evenings around design, material culture and cultural relevance.

Back to selected work

Registration pages, newsletters and visuals for two public evenings of a design editorial community. Future Bridge is the first event of the What Matters Platform series.

For guests who had been at Milan Design Week, the invitations went out as postcard-style emails rather than a newsletter blast. On the evenings themselves I coordinated on site and photographed the room.

The posters also ran as short motion loops, generated with AI video tools from the print designs.

Part II — Eindhoven · 06Living Lab 040 · Eindhoven

The Conscious Toolkit

A live toolkit website translating Living Lab 040 research into AutoCAD templates and Revit models for professionals.

Open live toolkitBack to selected work

Living Lab 040 tests sustainable housing on an urban site in Eindhoven, and most of its research sat in dense reports.

The toolkit turns that research into AutoCAD templates and Revit models professionals can open in their own software. The site is live.

A strategy challenge from the final semester of my second year at Fontys University of Applied Sciences.

Tomorrow’s Leadership in Art

A campaign concept against workplace bullying among senior men at Dutch companies, framed through a travelling art exhibition and VR simulation.

Open Canva designBack to selected work

A campaign concept against workplace bullying among senior men at Dutch companies. Instead of a lecture, the concept uses a travelling art exhibition with a VR simulation and workshops.

The project document positioned the campaign as a cultural intervention inside the workplace.

A project for a Social Psychology course at Fontys University of Applied Sciences, taking on workplace bullying rooted in sexism and misogyny among senior men.

Part I — Vienna · 01Tabasamu Austria · June 2026

Karaoke for a Good Cause

A zero-budget charity night at G5 Vienna for Tabasamu Austria — 160 guests, a live band, karaoke and a donation box.

View event photosBack to selected work

On 1 June 2026 our Event Marketing group ran Karaoke for a Good Cause at G5, under the U-Bahn arches in Vienna’s 19th district: a free-entry charity night for Tabasamu Austria, a non-profit that funds educational projects for children in East Africa. Karaoke, a live set by Elfsechzig, a lucky draw and a donation box at the door.

The constraint that shaped everything was money, because we had none. The whole evening ran as a zero-budget concept covered through sponsoring and partnerships — more than twenty companies contributed prizes or in-kind support — Raiffeisen Bank Austria, NEOH and many more — so every euro collected on the night went to the cause.

We aimed for 150 guests and counted around 160. With no media budget, the reach came from borrowed trust: one visual identity across poster, flyers and Instagram, carried by reposts from the band, the venue, the ÖH and Tabasamu itself.

A group project during the Event Marketing course at FHWien der WKW, Vienna. Photography by Claudy Visions.
